summary: Review eight material upstream changes across emulator determinism, disassembly-derived distribution builds, reconstruction validation, native Apple II probes, gameplay progress and retro-analysis tooling.
notes: The CPU audit queue contained zero unresolved source/target CPU areas. This pass therefore made no speculative CPU additions: Sim City output CPUs and all new minimum-hardware claims remain unknown where primary evidence was absent. No upstream software, disk image or emulator was built, launched or played by the tracker.

project.status: Primary source now includes seedable deterministic weak-bit and not-ready-drive noise for reproducible floppy-controller tests; independent build/run not performed.

identity.narrative: Hardware-level Rust Macintosh emulator with integrated disassembly, breakpoints, watchpoints, trap/history viewers and flux/bitstream disk support.

classification.narrative: Inspected IWM register/edge-driven controller code and compact-Mac bus implementation. README lists 128K through IIx/SE30/Portable/PowerBook models, 68000/68020/68030 and PMMU/FPU support. Peripherals and debugging establish a general research tool, not an application-specific wrapper. MIT licence for Snow; README acknowledges Musashi/MAME as reference and separately attributed components including Fluxfox and BlueSCSI Toolbox.

source_cpu.narrative: Documented source/input platforms: Macintosh. Processor scope: m68k.

target_cpu.narrative: No fixed target CPU is established; portability of the implementation language is not proof of supported architectures.

build.narrative: Upstream adds SetFloppyWeakBitsSeed and a serializable SplitMix64 path covering SWIM/IWM weak-bit zero sequences and per-drive not-ready garbage; clearing the seed restores nondeterministic behavior. This is a deterministic test-control feature, not an independent compatibility result. The tracker did not compile or run Snow.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The deterministic floppy-noise control adds no minimum host CPU, RAM or OS evidence, so no runtime profile is inferred.

ai.narrative: Bounded README and current commit inspection found no explicit development-AI attribution. This does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: New implementation with own hardware-level model and debugger; bounded screen found no tracked Snow equivalent. Source references are not a claim that Snow is a fork of MAME or Musashi.

project.status: ZX Spectrum disassembly now underpins v1.1.0 distribution builds for Aquarius+, Z88, Mitsubishi Multi 8, PC-8801 and SAM Coupé; tracker-side build/run not performed.
techniques: shared simulation with platform-specific display, input, sound and file layers

identity.narrative: The repository is now a multi-platform Sim City port rooted in the ZX Spectrum disassembly. The v1.1.0 distribution target packages separately documented Aquarius+, Z88, Mitsubishi Multi 8, PC-8801 and SAM Coupé outputs; these are one shared implementation, not separate projects.

classification.narrative: README documentation says the original simulation is retained while each machine rewrites screen, keyboard, sound and file handling. This is a disassembly-derived multi-platform port rather than analysis-only work.

source_cpu.narrative: The existing Z80 source-CPU decision remains tied to the inspected ZX Spectrum disassembly; the new ports do not change that historical input architecture.

target_cpu.narrative: The reviewed distribution and per-machine documentation establish output platforms but do not explicitly establish a processor architecture for every produced variant. No target CPU is inferred from platform names, z88dk or shared source.

build.narrative: The new Make dist target and make_dist.py create runnable distribution archives with machine-specific launch files and README material for Aquarius+, Z88, Mitsubishi Multi 8, PC-8801 and SAM Coupé; GitHub also publishes v1.1.0 as a multi-platform release. compilable/runnable are upstream-supported claims only: the tracker did not build, launch or play any package.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Per-platform documentation records media, display, audio and file-system behavior, but the reviewed change does not state verified minimum CPU, RAM, ROM or machine revisions. No runtime minimum is inferred.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI disclosure was found in the reviewed commit and distribution documentation; non-use is not established.

relationships.narrative: The five new output packages share the same repository, retained simulation and disassembly lineage. They remain one catalogue project rather than five inflated records.

project.status: 403 exact MAIN functions / 65,198 exact owned bytes and 97.54% reviewed MAIN CODE; shared OP/MAINL input producers now have separately bounded cold-product and guest-model validation without changing whole-game exactness.

identity.narrative: Scoped source recovery of MAIN, OP, MAINL and ZUN artifacts. README separates exact owned functions from source-present work and says whole-game reconstruction remains unfinished. The new candidates remain within the same scoped MAIN/OP/MAINL/ZUN recovery; neither controlled layout experiments nor candidate bodies expand the exact-function ledger.

classification.narrative: Scope: source-reconstruction / game. Primary README, repository file layout and selected implementation files were reviewed.

target_cpu.narrative: Target architecture x86. Host ports and minimum variants are not inferred from source CPU.

build.narrative: The new shared input source owns nine functions / 367 CODE bytes in each of OP and MAINL. Upstream reports two-source cold products reproducing 32 OP and 938 MAINL outputs plus independent 2,218-case-per-image guest models at two loads, with 19 mutations rejected per product. The author explicitly scopes this within each product and does not add whole-game byte percentage, canonical packed-file unit offsets or whole-product acceptance. The tracker did not compile, execute or byte-compare the revision.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The cold-product and guest-model checks are reconstruction evidence, not a verified minimum PC-98 runtime profile.

ai.narrative: Project-scoped agent instructions/configuration provide an AI-use signal; the particular agent is not inferred.

relationships.narrative: Checked current catalogue, source and decision URLs and related titles. Scoped source recovery of MAIN, OP, MAINL and ZUN artifacts. README separates exact owned functions from source-present work and says whole-game reconstruction remains unfinished.

project.status: Native Apple II collection; POM2 facade tests now exercise Apple //c and AppleMouse II firmware paths plus register, go and call control across game probes.

identity.narrative: The repository-level collection now includes the separately titled Wilderness reconstruction; it is retained within the established collection record rather than counted as a duplicate repository project.

classification.narrative: Neowilderness remains a reconstruction-informed subject inside the established mixed POM2 collection; its original-homebrew siblings are not relabelled as reverse-engineered.

source_cpu.narrative: The README and Snake header identify POM1 Apple-1/GEN2 versions as predecessors, and Chess documents reused POM1 rules code. Those predecessor files were not independently inspected, so no source CPU is inferred from the target assembly or Apple-1 label.

target_cpu.narrative: Arkabreakout’s game.s explicitly specifies NMOS 6502 and contains native gameplay assembly. ChromaBreak’s Makefile passes --cpu 65c02; boot.s starts with a 6502 CPU probe and then selects .setcpu "65C02", rejecting an NMOS IIe. These establish separate 6502 and 65C02 outputs, not a single machine minimum.

build.narrative: The POM2 facade delivery adds register/go/call controls and wires make test probes across Arkabreakout, Pinball and Wargalaga II. Arkabreakout's probe exercises Apple //c and card variants against AppleMouse II firmware, including detection, coordinates, launch/laser/menu input, suppression, DOS exit and display-mode invariants after each CPU instruction. These are upstream tests; the tracker did not build or run them.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The new real-firmware and //c probes strengthen test coverage but do not change the existing author-stated Apple II memory/storage profiles or establish a lower minimum.

ai.narrative: The facade merge is explicitly co-authored by Claude Opus 5.5, consistent with the existing project-level Claude attribution; this remains development evidence, separate from any in-game AI.

relationships.narrative: The Wilderness subtree documents reconstruction from external woz-a-day WOZ/A2R images kept out of git; this is a subject inside the tracked POM2 collection, not an original-homebrew relabel.

project.status: Early Amberstar reimplementation now integrates fight-or-flee choice, encounter triggering, battle outcomes, loot, defeated-monster removal and rescue/game-over handling; no complete-game claim.

identity.narrative: The shared Amber framework and Amberstar implementation remain one early reimplementation project. Current work adds an integrated encounter/battle/loot/defeat slice without claiming game completion.

classification.narrative: This remains direct C# gameplay and data-framework reimplementation, not recovered source or a binary-derived port claim.

source_cpu.narrative: Reviewed project documentation identifies legacy Atari ST, Amiga, DOS data or game heritage, but does not establish analyzed original CPU instructions; architecture is not inferred from the platform alone.

target_cpu.narrative: Reviewed source/build documentation names platforms or language/runtime but no explicit output CPU architecture; no target CPU is inferred from Java, C#, C/C++, or a portable framework.

build.narrative: Upstream adds fight-or-flee confirmation, chance-based fleeing, monster advantage, encounter activation when the party is reached, loot display, monster removal after victory, and Shandra rescue or game-over after defeat, with scenario tests and scripting commands. The tracker did not compile or play the project; build/run/play flags remain unknown.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The gameplay slice adds no explicit minimum host CPU, RAM, OS or mobile-device profile.

ai.narrative: The inspected commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5, supporting the existing Claude development attribution.

relationships.narrative: Exact root absent; related Ambermoon projects known, but Amberstar game and Amber framework are distinct work. Keep the shared framework and Amberstar under one root, separate from Ambermoon.net.

project.status: Released Apple II and Commodore ports plus buildable/testable Commander X16 target; current main adds AI playtesting infrastructure with seven isolated platform stages and a broad set of gameplay-parity fixes, without tracker-side execution.

identity.narrative: Moria8 is a single multi-platform assembly reimplementation of Moria. Current main contains released C64, C128, Plus/4 and Apple II outputs plus a new buildable/testable Commander X16 target; the README's status table still calls X16 planned, so it is not represented as a published release.

classification.narrative: This remains a native, platform-specific assembly reimplementation derived from the credited VMS Moria and Umoria lineages, not a reverse-engineered binary port.

source_cpu.narrative: The documented source lineages are VMS Pascal and C Umoria; no original executable ISA is established by the reviewed material, so source_cpu remains empty.

target_cpu.narrative: Existing Apple II and Commodore assembly supports the 6502 output. The Commander X16 makefile explicitly labels its new target 65C02/VERA, supporting the additional 65C02 output without inferring it from the platform name.

build.narrative: The merged playtesting work adds VICE binary-monitor sessions, goals, deterministic replay and a dashboard, then isolates fixed emulator ports with private network namespaces so seven platform stages (C64, C128, Plus/4, Apple II, Commander X16, Atari 8-bit and BBC Master) can run in parallel after one shared build. The same merge carries combat, item, monster and spell-effect fixes. These are upstream infrastructure and regression results; the tracker did not build or run any platform.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The existing Apple II 128 KiB/80-column/ProDOS profile remains sourced. Emulator-stage configuration and command timeouts are development-test requirements, not minimum physical hardware evidence, so no new runtime profile is added.

ai.narrative: The repository now documents an operational AI playtester using structured goals, sessions and deterministic replay. Existing Claude evidence remains the project-level development attribution; the infrastructure does not imply that every gameplay change was authored by a model.

relationships.narrative: The shared Commodore and Apple II ports remain one Moria8 project, distinct from its explicitly credited VMS Moria/Umoria ancestors. README/root license specify GPLv3, with disk data/LICENSE and source-offer material; artwork has separate creator credits. Future platform rows and unrelated Moria titles are not additional discoveries. The normalized root, title/alias and lineage screen found no same-code project in the 1,833-project baseline or expanded 2,249-root prior-review union.

project.status: v0.6.2 emulator/debugger; current main adds virtual-INF PRG autostart and fixes duplicate-sector FDC behavior, 16 MHz IPL timing, IKBD mouse-joystick drift, scripted mouse release and save-state safety.

identity.narrative: NeoST remains a chip-oriented ST/Mega ST/STE/Mega STE emulator and debugger. Current main adds --auto PRG launch through generated desktop INF data for TOS 1.04+, TOS 2.06 and EmuTOS; the author reports EMail 1.56 testing on an emulated 1 MiB monochrome ST, not a universal guest-compatibility claim.

classification.narrative: Reviewed the current primary source for classification.

source_cpu.narrative: Reviewed the current primary source for source_cpu.

target_cpu.narrative: The v0.6.2 release publishes explicit x86-64, ARM64 and WebAssembly output variants; these are host/output architectures, not minimum CPU generations.

build.narrative: The current change adds virtual-INF autostart and fixes FDC duplicate sector IDs, READ ADDRESS size/CRC placement, 16 MHz IPL-delay scaling and load-state consistency, IKBD $18 mouse-joystick drift, scripted mouse release timing and save-state refusal during virtual-INF reads. This is upstream test evidence only; the tracker did not build or run NeoST.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reported 1 MiB monochrome ST configuration for EMail 1.56 is an emulated guest test case, not a host minimum or a proven lowest compatible Atari configuration. Existing release-asset profiles remain unchanged.

ai.narrative: The inspected commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5, supporting the existing project-level development-AI attribution.

relationships.narrative: The current change does not resolve the existing predecessor, successor, fork and credited-source relationship gap.
relationships.next_action: Check predecessor, successor, fork and credited-source relationships.

project.status: Development head now recovers 65C816 JMP/JSR (abs,X) jump tables, stamps dispatch E/M/X width state on new targets and bounds or shrinks tables conservatively against real-ROM conflicts.

identity.narrative: Current README documents C64/C128/PET/NES machine loaders plus bundled SPC700 and 65C816 language variants; the display title now reflects both parts of the scope.

classification.narrative: The new 65816 Jump Tables analyzer remains core reverse-engineering tooling: it recovers computed-flow targets and disassembles handlers at the dispatch width without producing translated native output.

source_cpu.narrative: Machine descriptors explicitly cover 6502/6510/8502 inputs; README separately documents bundled SPC700 and 65C816 language variants for SNES code, with their current semantic limits preserved.

target_cpu.narrative: Ghidra analysis output is not a translated native retro binary.

build.narrative: Upstream adds a default-enabled analyzer for 65C816 JMP/JSR (abs,X) tables. It bounds tables using index masks, code/data occupancy, lowest targets and width-aware 16-instruction plausibility; shared tables are reused and later code conflicts shrink or withdraw over-read entries. Reported real-ROM rows increase decoded instructions and recover targets while reducing desync rate, with build-and-test and NES 35/35 gates passing. The tracker did not build Ghidra or run the corpora.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The analyzer change adds no minimum host CPU, RAM or OS evidence; Ghidra/JDK software prerequisites remain distinct from hardware minima.

ai.narrative: The implementation commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5 and links a Claude session; attribution is scoped to this analyzer change.

relationships.narrative: README says the extension was incubated in and serves CBongo/game-music-extraction; that adjacent multi-system extraction repository is queued for independent-scope review.
